title_guess: Cooperative banks in India: what they are, a village money example, the PCS / UCB / DCCB / SCB tiers and who regulates them
recurring_cast: token_square (yellow PCS, orange UCB, dark-green DCCB, light-green SCB; the same colours all video)
running_examples: village of 500 people: commercial bank pays 4% on deposits and lends at 12%

100 villagers pool 1 lakh each = 100 lakh in their own co-op bank; 4 lakh kept as CRR at 0%, 18 lakh in SLR bonds at 6%, 75 lakh lent to 25 members (3 lakh each) at 10%, 3 lakh expenses, 5% paid on deposits
tally: +7.5 lakh loan interest, +1.08 lakh bond interest, -3 lakh expenses, -5 lakh deposit interest = +58 thousand profit

best_moments.why: the 100-lakh pool is drawn as one bar cut into three coloured slices (lend / SLR / CRR); each slice is then routed to where it goes with its yield (CRR 4 lakh at 0%, SLR 18 lakh into a bond at 6%): reserves shown as parts of the same money
a green-income / pink-cost tally table sits under the full money-flow picture and ends in +58 thousand: members get better rates (5% vs 4%, 10% vs 12%) and the bank still breaks even
state -> district -> village as nested containers: two district frames full of PCS/UCB squares, one DCCB above each frame ('one per district'), one SCB on top ('one per state')
three regulator panels (grey RCS, yellow RBI, teal NABARD) each with the row of coloured squares it covers underneath (4, then 3, then 2): coverage readable at a glance
regulator x bank-type grid fills YES column by column into a staircase, then braces label UCB 'dual control' and DCCB/SCB 'triple control'
mirror comparison: co-op loop (community starts bank, bank serves the same community) beside a commercial bank where a small shareholder group owns it and a much bigger public crowd is served

weak_moments.why: about 80 s on one canvas where the only change is a cream highlight moving down a four-item 'promotes' list; plus a long members paragraph at left
UCB facts arrive as a note box, a conditions list and a members card: text-heavy, the only picture is a small licence icon
who-serves-whom is told by three tinted text notes hung off the tree instead of service arrows moving down it
the Registrar's role is a six-item text list of managerial areas

segments.teaches: a cooperative bank is started by a local community for itself and gives its members deposits, loans and other services; members share a common bond (place, profession or interest)

elements.what: dense crowd labelled local community
'starts' arrow from the crowd to the bank mark
red round cooperative-bank logo labelled BANK
elbow arrow from the bank back to the crowd labelled banking services
three teal bullets: deposits, loans, other services
light-blue panel framing the loop, 'Co-operative bank' heading above
'members' paragraph on the left with a pointer line into the panel

segments.notes: 5 change events (~every 9 s). The closed loop (community -> bank -> same community) is the core picture: owners and customers are the same crowd.
segments.idea: the people who start a cooperative bank are the same people it serves
segments.shown_as: a crowd labelled local community sends a 'starts' arrow to a bank mark; an elbow arrow returns from the bank to the same crowd labelled banking services, with deposits, loans and other services listed under it; a blue panel frames the loop and a members paragraph attaches from the left

segments.teaches: its objective is to serve members, not to maximise profit; it promotes democratic participation, financial inclusion, economic development and local needs

elements.what: 'objective' heading and line under the panel, then 'profit is not the goal' with 'not' in red
'promotes' list of four items at right
cream band lighting each 'promotes' item in turn

segments.notes: Only 2 change events in 83 s (~every 42 s). The additions are teacher-board style (L1): plain text with a moving highlighter on top of the earlier L2 loop.
segments.idea: a co-op bank exists for its members' good, not for profit
segments.shown_as: an objective line writes on under the loop, then a short line with a red 'not' rules out profit; at right a four-item 'promotes' list appears and each item is lit with a cream band as it is spoken

segments.teaches: a commercial bank is owned by shareholders, serves the general public and aims at profit, unlike a co-op bank

elements.what: co-op panel shrinks into the left half; a vertical divider drops
small group labelled shareholders
'own' arrow from shareholders to the commercial-bank logo
commercial bank logo (blue and red square)
'banking services' arrow down to a much larger crowd labelled general public
objective line: profit maximisation, in bold

segments.notes: 4 change events (~every 7 s). Owners vs users shown by crowd size alone; the objective lines mirror each other ('not profit' vs 'profit').
segments.idea: in a commercial bank the few owners and the many customers are different people, and profit is the goal
segments.shown_as: the co-op loop shrinks to the left half and a divider drops; on the right a small shareholder group sends an 'own' arrow to a bank mark, which sends 'banking services' down to a much bigger general-public crowd; its objective line says profit, mirroring the co-op's 'not profit'

segments.teaches: village example: a commercial bank takes deposits at 4% and lends at 12%; 100 villagers instead pool 1 lakh each (100 lakh) into their own co-op bank; of it, CRR 4 lakh is kept at 0% and SLR 18 lakh goes into bonds at 6%; the rest is free to lend

elements.what: round village scene (hills, sun, trees) over a crowd labelled 500 people
commercial bank logo
green elbow arrow carrying a banknote: deposits 4%
red elbow loop back carrying a banknote: loan 12%
cream '100 people' tag branching off the 500
'100 people x 1 lakh' beside a blue vertical bar
banknote arrow into the co-op bank logo
horizontal 100-lakh bar in three colours: blue available for lending, yellow SLR, green CRR
curved arrow from the CRR slice to '4 lakh @ 0%'
green bond certificate fed by the SLR slice, labelled '18 lakh @ 6%'

segments.notes: 16 change events (~every 5 s): the densest, most visual stretch. Banking saancha: one deposit pool drawn as a bar cut into lend / SLR / CRR slices, each slice then routed to its home with its yield. Check: 75 + 18 + 4 + 3 = 100 lakh.
segments.idea: villagers can pool savings into their own bank, but part of the pool must be parked as CRR and SLR before the rest is lent
segments.shown_as: a village scene with '500 people' sends a green deposit arrow carrying a banknote to a commercial bank at 4% and gets a red loan loop back at 12%; a '100 people x 1 lakh' block splits off and a banknote arrow carries it to the co-op bank; under the bank a 100-lakh bar appears in three coloured slices (lend / SLR / CRR); a curved arrow takes the CRR slice to '4 lakh @ 0%' and another drops the SLR slice into a bond certificate marked '18 lakh @ 6%'
segments.example: 500 villagers; commercial bank 4% deposit / 12% loan; 100 x 1 lakh = 100 lakh; CRR 4 lakh @ 0%; SLR 18 lakh in bonds @ 6%

segments.teaches: the co-op lends 75 lakh to 25 members (3 lakh each) at 10%, spends 3 lakh on expenses and pays its depositors 5%

elements.what: '25 people' label branching off the 100 members
red elbow loan arrow with a banknote from the co-op bank up to the 25, marked 10% and '3 lakh each'
the blue 'lend' slice forks into 'loan 75 lakh @ 10%' and 'expenses 3 lakh'
green '5%' added on the members' deposit arrow into the co-op bank

segments.notes: 5 change events (~every 8 s). Both banks' rates now sit on one canvas, so 5% vs 4% and 10% vs 12% can be compared by eye.
segments.idea: the co-op lends to its own members more cheaply (10% vs 12%) and pays them more on deposits (5% vs 4%)
segments.shown_as: a '25 people' label branches off the members and a red loan arrow with a banknote climbs from the co-op bank to them, marked 10% and '3 lakh each'; the blue lend slice of the bar forks into '75 lakh @ 10%' and '3 lakh expenses'; the deposit arrow into the co-op bank gains a green 5% tag, opposite the commercial bank's 4% and 12%
segments.example: 25 borrowers x 3 lakh = 75 lakh at 10%; expenses 3 lakh; deposit rate 5%

segments.teaches: income (7.5 lakh loan interest + 1.08 lakh bond interest) minus costs (3 lakh expenses + 5 lakh deposit interest) leaves a 58 thousand profit: small, but members are better off

elements.what: tally at lower right: two green income rows and two pink cost rows with signed amounts
rule line then 'profit = +58 thousand'

segments.notes: 2 change events in 60 s (~every 30 s): the tally appears, then the canvas holds while the narrator explains. Income green, cost pink: sign shown by colour.
segments.idea: even after giving members better rates, the co-op covers its costs with a small profit
segments.shown_as: a tally table pops in under the money-flow picture: two green income rows (loan interest, bond interest) and two pink cost rows (expenses, deposit interest); a rule is drawn and 'profit = +58 thousand' is written under it, with every source amount still visible above

segments.teaches: cooperative credit has three tiers; tier 1 holds primary credit societies (rural and urban areas) whose members are small farmers, rural artisans, farm labourers and other rural residents, and which give them credit

elements.what: three stacked blue bands labelled tier 3, tier 2, tier 1 (tier 1 thicker)
yellow square marked PCS in tier 1
PCS forks to 'rural areas' and 'urban areas'
grey members card with four member groups
elbow arrow labelled credit from PCS down to the members card
orange UCB square placed in tier 1 beside PCS

segments.notes: 7 change events (~every 6 s). Empty upper bands promise what is coming: a 'slots to fill' device. Colour per institution type is fixed from here to the end.
segments.idea: the bottom tier is the local credit society, which lends to small rural members
segments.shown_as: three empty blue bands stack up labelled tier 3, 2, 1; a yellow square marked PCS drops into the bottom band, forks to rural and urban areas, and an elbow arrow labelled credit runs from it down to a grey card of member groups; an orange UCB square takes the other slot in tier 1

segments.teaches: urban cooperative banks (also tier 1) have no area limit (rural to metro), may work across states if RBI conditions are met (track record, RBI rules, minimum net worth), serve traders, salaried people, MSMEs, small entrepreneurs and professionals, and hold a banking licence

elements.what: under UCB: 'no area limit' pointing to four area types
cream NOTE box at top right on working in many states
three condition bullets under the note
grey members card for UCB with five member groups
elbow arrow labelled banking services from UCB to its members card
small bank-licence certificate clipped onto the UCB square

segments.notes: 10 change events (~every 8 s), nearly all text. Quiet contrast: PCS has a 'credit' arrow, UCB a 'banking services' arrow, i.e. PCS only lends while UCB does full banking.
segments.idea: a UCB is a full bank for town members, can spread across areas and states, and needs an RBI licence
segments.shown_as: under the orange UCB square 'no area limit' points to four area types; a cream note box at top right adds multi-state working with three condition bullets; a grey members card hangs under UCB on a 'banking services' elbow arrow; finally a small licence certificate clips onto the UCB square

segments.teaches: a primary credit society in an urban area can start working as a UCB by taking a banking licence from RBI

elements.what: dotted arrow from the PCS square to the UCB square
licence certificate under UCB
short line under PCS explaining the licence route

segments.notes: 2 change events. The notes and member cards clear first. Upgrade shown only by a dotted arrow; BIE could recolour the yellow square to orange as the licence stamps on.
segments.idea: a society can upgrade into a bank by getting an RBI licence
segments.shown_as: the cards clear, leaving PCS and UCB squares in tier 1 with the licence under UCB; a dotted arrow travels from the PCS square to the UCB square and a short line under PCS explains the licence route

segments.teaches: in each district many PCS and UCBs sit under one District Central Cooperative Bank (tier 2); in each state one State Cooperative Bank sits on top (tier 3)

elements.what: tier bands enlarged to fill the screen
two black-framed DISTRICT boxes in tier 1, each filled with a row of mixed yellow PCS and orange UCB squares
dark-green DCCB square in tier 2 above each district, with an up-arrow from the district box and a 'one per district' tag
light-green SCB square alone in tier 3 with a 'one per state' tag

segments.notes: 7 change events (~every 4 s). Banking saancha for state -> district -> village: nested frames + counts ('one per district', 'one per state') + one colour per tier.
segments.idea: co-op banks nest: many local units per district feed one district bank, and one state bank sits above all districts
segments.shown_as: the tier bands zoom up to fill the screen; two black district frames fill with rows of yellow PCS and orange UCB squares; a dark-green DCCB square appears in tier 2 above each frame with an up-arrow from it, tagged one per district; a light-green SCB square lands alone in tier 3, tagged one per state
segments.example: two districts with 5-6 PCS/UCB squares each; one DCCB per district; one SCB per state

segments.teaches: the SCB serves the DCCBs; each DCCB serves the PCS and UCBs in its district; UCBs serve their members and PCS in their district

elements.what: SCB -> 'many' DCCB -> forks to 'many' PCS and 'many' UCB, using the same coloured squares
three tinted note boxes on dotted leader lines, each matching its square's colour

segments.notes: 6 change events (~every 10 s). Same colour coding as the tiers, so the tree reads as the tiers turned into a family tree.
segments.idea: services flow down the chain: state bank -> district bank -> local societies and town banks
segments.shown_as: the bands vanish and the coloured squares regroup into a vertical tree: SCB at top, a down-arrow marked many to DCCB, which forks to many PCS and many UCB; three tinted note boxes, each in its square's colour, hang off the levels on dotted leader lines

segments.teaches: all co-op banks are registered and governed under their state's Cooperative Societies Act; the state's Registrar of Cooperative Societies controls managerial matters (registration, management, administration, recruitment, amalgamation, liquidation) for PCS, UCB, DCCB and SCB

elements.what: grey panel holding the regulator picture
law scroll with an emblem, dotted line up to STATE and a pointer naming the state act
four arrows converging up from the PCS, UCB, DCCB and SCB squares onto the law icon
caption: all co-op banks registered under the state act
big '?' beside the law icon
grey government building labelled RCS (registrar)
six managerial areas in two columns, with the four squares in a row below

segments.notes: 6 change events (~every 11 s). The '?' next to the law sets up 'who enforces it?' and the RCS building answers it.
segments.idea: each state's co-op law and its Registrar run the management side of all co-op banks
segments.shown_as: four coloured squares send arrows converging up onto a law-scroll icon inside a grey panel, with a dotted line up to STATE and a pointer naming the state act; a big '?' appears beside the law and is answered by a grey government building labelled RCS; the panel then moves to the top-left with the law above it, a six-item managerial-control list and the four squares beneath

segments.teaches: RBI regulates banking matters for UCBs, DCCBs and SCBs under the Banking Regulation Act 1949; NABARD inspects DCCBs and SCBs for financial health and compliance

elements.what: yellow panel with the RBI emblem, 'regulates banking matters' under it
row of three squares (UCB, DCCB, SCB) under the RBI panel
law icon for the 1949 banking act, joined to RBI by an arrow
teal panel with the NABARD emblem, 'inspects financial health and compliance' under it
row of two squares (DCCB, SCB) under the NABARD panel
RBI and NABARD emblems

segments.notes: 6 change events (~every 14 s). Three regulator columns side by side; the rows of squares under each shrink 4 -> 3 -> 2, which shows coverage without words.
segments.idea: three regulators split the job (state registrar manages, RBI regulates banking, NABARD inspects), and each covers a different set of co-op banks
segments.shown_as: a yellow RBI panel and then a teal NABARD panel open to the right of the grey RCS panel; under each, the regulator's job writes on and a row of the coloured squares it covers is laid out (four under RCS, three under RBI, two under NABARD); a law icon for the 1949 banking act attaches to RBI by an arrow

segments.teaches: PCS is under the state registrar only; UCB is under two regulators (dual control); DCCB and SCB are under three (triple control)

elements.what: columns headed by the RCS building, RBI and NABARD icons; four blue rows, one per coloured square; YES cells
brace + 'dual regulatory control' beside the UCB row
long brace + 'triple regulatory control' beside the DCCB and SCB rows

segments.notes: 5 change events (~every 7 s). An app-promo overlay covers the lower left at about 755-758 s; ignore it.
segments.idea: the number of regulators grows as you go up the co-op ladder
segments.shown_as: the three regulator icons line up as column heads over four blue rows, one per coloured square; YES marks fill in column by column so they form a staircase (1, 2, 3, 3 per row); a short brace marks UCB as dual control and a long brace marks DCCB and SCB as triple control
segments.example: regulators per type: PCS 1, UCB 2, DCCB 3, SCB 3
